title: Building homemade banjo, guitar and bass as a boy
summary: At about seven Ory made a banjo from a bucket, strung with thread and fishing line, and a cigar-box guitar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: What I'd like to know from you first is how you first became interested in music. How old you were and what you were playing and so on. Well, I was about seven years old. About seven years old. And you were still in Laplace?
Now what instrument did you play?
Well, I first made a banjo. Yeah. And I made a ghetto.
You mean you built them yourself?
Yeah. And I made a bass.
A ghetto. She must put the all in.
You know what you're talking about.

What kind of banjo did you make? I made a five-string banjo. Out of what? Out of ten buckets. Mm-mm. About the banjo. Yeah, the banjo was a cut bucket, half of it down in regular buckets, you know, about this size. And cut it down about there. Yeah. Well, that was the first one. That was the first one, yeah.
And you used the metal strings on that one.
No, I was using thread and fishing cards and...
Oh, yeah. Because they broke all the time. Yeah. When I made one loose. Out of a cigar box later on. No, a cigar box was the guitar. Oh, excuse me.
